title: Sir Nicholas Throckmorton to the Regent Moray, Greenwich, 20 July 1569, BL Add MS 33531 ff. 79-80 (DECODE R8348)

steps.what: Bain, Calendar of Scottish Papers ii, grepped for 'fol. 79': no. 1103, Throckmorton to Murray, 20 July 1569, Add MS 33531 f. 79, '3 pp. In cipher deciphered', addressed 'Lorde Regent of Scotlande'.
Cryptiana mary.htm: 'Throckmorton-Moray Cipher (1569)', f.79r-80v, key reconstructed.
Fetched the 4 DECODE images and the DOC_ key image with the shared cookie.
Read the date on f. 80v: 'At Grenew. the 20th of July 1569' (DECODE has 26 Jul).

Decoded about twenty cipher words with Tomokiyo's key and matched them to the interlinear gloss (and, the, your, frends, intended, resolved, concerning, restauration, disposition, aforesaid, condescend, should, Liddington).

Read every cipher passage of ff. 79r, 79v, 80r and the signature from half-line crops of the full-resolution scans, decoding by hand with Tomokiyo's key; checked against the surviving gloss. Name signs Z, M, La and a handful of words left uncertain.

outcome.method_basis: Every cipher passage was decoded by hand with Tomokiyo's reconstruction of the Throckmorton-Moray key (cryptiana mary.htm, filed on the DECODE record R8348 in 2024), because the contemporary interlinear decipherment is half faded by a water stain; the surviving gloss served as a check.
outcome.notes: Read at the time and calendared by Bain (no. 1103) in summary only; the stain-faded decipherment is replaced here by a full reading from the cipher (reading.md, write-up throck1569.html). Sender identified, DECODE date corrected to 20 July. Name signs Z, M, La unresolved. Catalogue entry 83 removed.

prior.where: contemporary interlinear decipherment on the leaf; calendared in Bain, Calendar of Scottish Papers ii (1900) no. 1103; key reconstructed by Tomokiyo (cryptiana mary.htm) and filed on DECODE R8348 (18 Sept 2024)

human: Project-level: obtained a DECODE login with privileges and passed its session cookie to the model, set up Claude Code with Opus 5, and posed the problem with /goal. No target-specific intervention recorded.
